coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Channel Mission Bay
record.summary: Channel Mission Bay is a 315-unit apartment building (per its DBI permit) at 185 Channel St in Mission Bay, developed by DOB Mission Bay LP with design/development by LaHue and Associates and listed by UDR as one of its communities. DBI records permit #201104224606 (8 stories, 315 units) as completed on July 22, 2014; DataSF Assessor tax-roll data are consistent with that: assessed improvement value rose from $0 in the 2012 roll to $30M in 2013 and $94M in 2014, with 316 units first recorded in the 2015 roll.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is the union of Assessor lots 8711023B and 8711023C (8,375 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8711023)); 96% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 73% of the lot.

changes.text: Channel Mission Bay now uses its Assessor lot lines.

The record now says the city's building permit for the 315-unit building is recorded complete on July 22, 2014 (DataSF), rather than that no source states a completion date, and notes that a completed permit is not an opening date. Developer, design firm and UDR are cited to their own pages. The Gus's Community Market entry no longer claims a deli, butcher counter or cafe or a Channel Mission Bay ground-floor location, which the CBS article does not state; Gus's own site now backs the 1101 4th St address and current operation. The Market Hall's 2016 opening year could not be checked because its only source is an unreadable Yelp listing, and a 2014 SFist piece shows it was planned for Labor Day 2014, so the record now lists this as an open question. The Wikimedia photo credit no longer names a flight the file page does not state.

changes.text: CBS News SF reported that Wednesday, Dec 26, 2018 was opening day for the family's fourth grocery store, Gus's Community Market in Mission Bay. Gus's own website lists its Mission Bay Market at 1101 4th St, at 4th and Channel. The CBS article gives no address and does not describe a deli, butcher counter or cafe, so those details and the ground-floor location in the Channel Mission Bay building are not stated here.

The Market Hall, a 10,000 sq ft gourmet grocery and food hall from Primo Hospitality Group, opened at 1101 4th St in the Channel Mission Bay building's ground floor in 2016; its Yelp listing now shows it closed, though no closure date was found. Gus's Community Market later opened in the same unit.

open_questions: DBI records permit #201104224606 as completed on 2014-07-22 (DataSF i98e-djp9), but a permit completion is not an opening date; no source found states when the building opened or first leased.

This parcel's own DataSF Assessor 'year_property_built' field is blank in every roll year checked -- unlike most other Mission Bay buildings checked, the Assessor does not give a direct construction year for this parcel.

Several real-estate listing aggregators (Zillow, Trulia, Apartments.com) state the building was 'built in 2013,' which is consistent with the Assessor's value trend, but these pages could not be checked and their exact wording is not confirmed, so that claim is not used as a citation here.

The building's developer (DOB Mission Bay LP) and the LaHue and Associates/UDR project pages already cited for this record do not themselves give an opening date, and no other source found confirms the opening year.

The Market Hall's opening year is not shown. Pier & Point's earlier retail list gave 2016, which rested on a Yelp listing that could not be opened (HTTP 403 again on 2026-10-12). SFist (2014-06-09) reported it as planned for 185 Channel Street with a target of Labor Day 2014. No source read states when it opened or closed, so its closed status also rests on the unread Yelp listing. Gus's Community Market's own site lists a Mission Bay Market at 1101 4th St (at 4th and Channel), read 2026-09-29.
